editorial:
TechCrunch’s “3 key metrics for cybersecurity product managers” is a blunt reminder that most PMs are still chasing a handful of hard‑numbers, not a dozen glossy AI dashboards. The piece’s focus on user‑impact, adoption, and reliability scores cuts through the noise of every new AI‑generated metric that promises insight but delivers distraction.

The broader conversation is louder still. Stratechery’s deep dive on Stripe’s OpenRouter acquisition shows how AI is being woven into core business models, yet Ben Thompson warns the real value comes from solving concrete customer problems, not from deploying every shiny model under the sun. At the same time, a Substack essay titled “Product Managers are becoming AI Agent Managers” argues that the proliferation of autonomous agents is turning PMs into overseers of bots rather than architects of outcomes. The common thread? Metrics are exploding, but decision quality is eroding. The answer isn’t more data; it’s disciplined metric hygiene—pick the few signals that directly tie to user value, and let AI handle the rest.

Senior PMs, this is where your daily grind meets strategic impact. You own the feature roadmap, translate executive ambition into sprint‑level goals, and are the bridge between data engineers and design. Insist on a metric charter that caps new KPIs to those that can be traced back to a user story or a clear revenue impact. Push back on every AI‑generated dashboard that can’t answer the “so what?” question, and work with your analytics team to automate collection of the core signals you’ve approved. By guarding the signal‑to‑noise ratio, you preserve your credibility with leadership and keep the product team focused on outcomes, not illusion.
key_takeaways: PMs must prune metric bloat to preserve decision quality.
AI should automate data collection, not dictate strategic direction.
Leadership credibility hinges on linking every KPI to a user outcome.

must_reads.title: 3 key metrics for cybersecurity product managers
must_reads.why: The piece cuts through AI hype by zeroing in on the three numbers that actually move the needle for security products, a reminder that breadth isn’t a substitute for depth.

must_reads.title: Stripe Acquiring OpenRouter, Aggregating AI, Flipping the Business Model
must_reads.why: Ben Thompson shows that AI integrations succeed only when they solve a real pain point, debunking the myth that every AI feature is a strategic win.

must_reads.title: Product Managers are becoming AI Agent Managers
must_reads.why: The author warns that without a clear metric guardrail, PMs risk becoming mere supervisors of bots, diluting their strategic influence.

contrarian.note: Claims autonomous AI agents can replace many PM decision loops, implying the PM role will shrink to oversight of bots.
contrarian.title: AI Agents for Product Managers: What They Are Really Good For

pm_homework: Audit your current KPI dashboard and cut any metric that can’t be tied to a specific user outcome.
Draft a one‑page AI‑tool charter that defines which decisions stay human‑owned and which can be delegated to automation.
